st: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Cook the onions for 12 minutes until deep brown.
Add the lamb and brown it on all sides for 8 minutes.
Add [[3 cups]] water, [[1 tsp]] cumin and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer for 60 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Lift out the lamb. Measure the broth and add water to reach [[4 cups]]. Keep the lamb warm.
Bring the broth to a boil, add the soaked rice, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] cumin. Boil for 5 minutes until the water level drops to the rice.
Bury the lamb in the rice. Cover tightly with foil under the lid and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt [[2 tbsp]] sugar in a skillet over medium heat until amber. Add the carrots and a splash of water and cook for 5 minutes until just tender.
Stir in the raisins and cardamom for 1 minute.
Heap the rice on a platter, place the lamb on top, and cover with the carrots, raisins and almonds.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, then add about [[1 cup]] warm water to form a firm dough. Knead 8 minutes, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, one minced onion, [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper and coriander for the filling.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the other onion for 6 minutes. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste and lentils with [[2 cups]] water. Simmer 30 minutes until the lentils are soft, for the sauce.
Mash the garlic with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and mix into the yogurt.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 4-inch squares.
Put [[1 tbsp]] filling in the center of each square. Pinch the opposite corners together over the filling to seal into a pouch.
Oil a steamer rack. Arrange the dumplings in one layer and steam over boiling water for 20 minutes until the meat reaches 160°F (71°C). Work in batches.
Plate the mantu, spoon on the garlic yogurt, then the lentil sauce, and sprinkle with dried mint.

ing: white and light green parts, finely chopped
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and about [[1 cup]] warm water into a firm dough. Knead 8 minutes and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet. Cook the leeks with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper flakes for 10 minutes until very soft. Cool.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 3-inch circles or squares. Put [[1 tbsp]] leek filling on each, fold into half moons and press the edges shut.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, add the beef and cook 8 minutes until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, coriander and [[1 tsp]] salt, plus [[1 cup]] water. Simmer 20 minutes for the meat sauce.
Mash the garlic with a pinch of salt and mix into the yogurt.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 6 minutes until they float and the dough is tender. Drain.
Spread garlic yogurt on a platter, lay the dumplings on top, spoon over the meat sauce and sprinkle with [[1 tbsp]] dried mint.

ing: divided, for the dough and frying
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[2 tbsp]] oil and about [[1 cup]] warm water into a soft dough. Knead 8 minutes, then cover and rest 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until soft, drain, and mash.
Mix the mash with the leeks, cilantro, chili, coriander and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a thin 8-inch circle.
Spread filling over half of each circle, fold the other half over, and press the edges to seal.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook each bolani for 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp, adding oil as needed.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with yogurt.
In a large bowl, mix the beef, onion, tomatoes, chilies, cilantro, crushed coriander, cumin and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Add the egg and [[3 tbsp]] flour and knead by hand for 3 minutes until sticky and well blended.
Cover and chill for 30 minutes so the patties hold together.
Wet your hands and shape the meat into 8 flat patties about 4 inches wide and 0.5 inch thick.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Fry 3 or 4 patties at a time for 5 minutes per side until deep brown and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Drain on paper towels and fry the second batch with the remaining oil.
Serve hot with flatbread, chutney and sliced onion.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 12 minutes until golden brown.
Add the lamb and brown it for 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, turmeric, coriander, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper for 1 minute.
Add [[2 cups]] water, cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until it wilts.
Add the cilantro and dill and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, until the greens are dark and the oil rises to the top.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice and taste for salt.
Serve with rice or flatbread.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the beef and cook 8 minutes until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Add [[2 cloves]] of the garlic, the tomatoes, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Cook 5 minutes.
Pour in [[8 cups]] water and add the beans and chickpeas. Simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the broken noodles and cook 8 minutes until tender.
Mix the yogurt with the last garlic clove and a pinch of salt.
Stir half of the dill into the soup and taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with a spoonful of garlic yogurt.
Sprinkle with the remaining dill and serve hot.
Sprinkle the eggplant slices with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and let them sit for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplant in batches for 3 minutes per side until golden. Set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
Add [[2 cloves]] garlic, the turmeric, tomatoes, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste and [[0.5 cup]] water. Simmer 12 minutes until saucy.
Return the eggplant to the pan, spoon sauce over it, cover and cook 8 minutes on low.
Mix the yogurt with [[2 cloves]] garlic and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Spread some garlic yogurt on a platter, layer the eggplant and sauce on top, and add more yogurt.
Sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] dried mint and serve with bread.
Stir [[1 tsp]] sugar and the yeast into [[1.5 cups]] warm water and let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix [[4 cups]] flour and [[2 tsp]] salt in a large bowl. Add the yeast water and [[2 tbsp]] oil and mix into a soft dough.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 60 minutes until doubled.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking sheet or stone inside.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces and stretch each into a long oval about 0.5 inch thick.
Press your fingers down the length in rows to make ridges, brush with oil and sprinkle with [[1 tbsp]] nigella and [[1 tbsp]] sesame seeds.
Bake 1 or 2 loaves at a time on the hot sheet for 8 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Wrap in a cloth to keep soft and serve warm.
Whisk [[0.33 cup]] cornstarch with [[0.5 cup]] cold milk until smooth with no lumps.
Heat [[4 cups]] milk with [[0.5 cup]] sugar in a heavy saucepan over medium heat until steaming.
Pour in the cornstarch mixture slowly while whisking constantly.
Cook for 8 minutes, stirring without stopping, until the pudding is thick and coats the spoon.
Stir in [[1 tsp]] cardamom and [[1 tbsp]] rose water and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour into six small bowls.
Cool for 15 minutes at room temperature, then chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Top with [[0.25 cup]] pistachios before serving.
Whisk [[1 tbsp]] cornstarch into [[0.5 cup]] of the milk until smooth.
Heat the rest of the milk (about [[1.5 cups]]) with [[0.75 cup]] sugar and a pinch of salt in a saucepan until steaming.
Whisk in the cornstarch mix and cook for 5 minutes over medium heat until slightly thickened. Do not boil hard.
Remove from the heat and stir in the cardamom and [[1 tbsp]] rose water.
Cool the mixture for 30 minutes, then chill in the fridge for 2 hours until very cold.
Stir in [[2 cups]] heavy cream.
Churn in an ice cream maker for 25 minutes, or pour into a freezer container.
Fold in [[0.33 cup]] pistachios. If not churned, stir the container every hour for 3 hours.
Freeze until firm, about 3 hours, then scoop and serve.
Put [[2 cups]] yogurt in a large pitcher.
Add [[0.5 cup]] cold water and whisk until smooth and pourable.
Stir in the grated cucumber.
Add [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] dried mint and stir well.
Slowly pour in [[2 cups]] cold sparkling water and stir gently so it stays fizzy.
Taste and add a little more salt or mint if needed.
Chill 20 minutes if you have time, then pour over ice and serve.
